title: The Wolf and the Goat
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Wolf caught sight of a Goat browsing above him on the scanty herbage that grew on the top of a steep rock; and being unable to get at her, tried to induce her to come lower down. "You are risking your life up there, madam, indeed you are," he called out: "pray take my advice and come down here, where you will find plenty of better food." The Goat turned a knowing eye upon him. "It's little you care whether I get good grass or bad," said she: "what you want is to eat me."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the Goat browsing when the Wolf saw her?
options: On the scanty herbage at the top of a steep rock
In a meadow beside a stream
Near the entrance of the Wolf's den
Inside a shepherd's pen

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the Wolf try to induce the Goat to come lower down?
options: Because he was unable to get at her where she stood
Because he wanted her to meet the other goats
Because he feared the rock would collapse
Because the herbage above was actually poisonous

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what warning does the Wolf give the Goat about her position?
options: That she is risking her life up there
That the weather will soon turn stormy
That other wolves are approaching
That the rock is not safe to stand on for long

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf claim she will find if she comes down?
options: Plenty of better food
A safer place to sleep
Company from other goats
Protection from other predators

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Goat look at the Wolf as she responds?
options: With a knowing eye
With a frightened glance
With complete indifference
With tears in her eyes

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Goat say the Wolf actually wants?
options: To eat her
To steal her food
To trap her on the rock forever
To lead her to the other goats

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Goat say it's little the Wolf cares whether she gets good grass or bad?
options: She recognizes that his concern for her food is only a cover for his real, harmful intention
She believes the Wolf genuinely dislikes grass of any kind
She thinks the Wolf is testing her to see if she trusts him
She has heard rumors that the Wolf never eats grass himself

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Advice offered by someone who stands to benefit from it should be viewed with suspicion
Goats are naturally braver than wolves in dangerous situations
Steep rocks are always the safest place for goats to graze
Wolves are incapable of climbing steep terrain

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf call the Goat when he speaks to her?
options: Madam
My dear friend
Little one
Neighbour

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf say he is offering the Goat?
options: His advice
His protection
His company
His share of food

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what kind of herbage is said to grow on top of the rock where the Goat stands?
options: Scanty herbage
Rich, abundant herbage
Herbage unlike any found below
No herbage at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the phrase "a knowing eye" suggest about the Goat's reaction to the Wolf?
options: She immediately sees through his flattering words to his real motive
She is confused about what the Wolf actually wants from her
She admires the Wolf's cleverness in offering such advice
She is too distracted by the food below to notice the danger

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "induce" mean in "tried to induce her to come lower down"?
options: Persuade or lead someone to do something
Physically force someone to move
Frighten someone into fleeing
Trick someone using a disguise

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Wolf tries to lure a Goat down from safety with false concern, but she sees through his true motive
A Wolf and Goat share the same patch of grass peacefully
A Goat climbs down willingly and is caught by the Wolf
A Wolf warns a Goat about a real danger on the rock above her
